chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Udaym ibn al-Ḥurr, who said:
I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying:

Indeed, Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام instructed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding all of the prayers, and he assigned for every salat (prayer) two times, except al-Maghrib, for he assigned for it one single time.

key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, the angel who conveyed divine instruction
key_terms.رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.وَقْتَيْنِ: two designated times for a prayer

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the prayer times taught by Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام taught the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم the prescribed prayer times. It indicates that each salat (prayer) has two designated times, except Maghrib, which has one specific time, making it significant in discussions of prayer timings in fiqh.
